Shiny module for data editing

Source: R/dataEdit.R
dataEdit.Rd

dataEdit renders an editable, spreadsheet-like grid built on the MIT-licensed 'Tabulator' JavaScript library. Edits are sent to R as cell-level changes rather than whole tables, which keeps large datasets responsive and makes undo/redo, change tracking and database commits possible.

Usage

dataEditUI(
  id,
  height = "65vh",
  toolbar = TRUE,
  toolbar_left = NULL,
  toolbar_right = NULL
)

dataEditServer(
  id,
  data = reactive(NULL),
  col_bind = NULL,
  col_edit = TRUE,
  col_options = NULL,
  col_stretch = FALSE,
  col_names = TRUE,
  col_readonly = NULL,
  col_hide = NULL,
  col_factor = FALSE,
  row_bind = NULL,
  row_edit = TRUE,
  row_index = reactive(NULL),
  rows = NULL,
  columns = NULL,
  quiet = FALSE,
  read_fun = "read.csv",
  read_args = NULL,
  track = NULL,
  code_name = "data",
  ...
)

Arguments

id

unique identifier for the module to prevent namespace clashes when making multiple calls to this shiny module.

height

height of the grid as a valid CSS unit, set to "65vh" by default.

toolbar

logical indicating whether the toolbar (undo/redo, columns, find, review changes, code), review panel and status bar should be shown around the grid, set to TRUE by default.

toolbar_left, toolbar_right

optional UI elements to add at the start or end of the toolbar (data_edit() adds its Open and Export menus here).

data

a reactive expression containing an array (e.g. data.frame, matrix or data.table), a database table (see db_table) or a vector indicating the dimensions of the array (e.g. c(10,10)) or column names to construct a new template for editing. If no data is supplied a template with 10 rows and columns will be generated for editing.

col_bind

additional columns to add to the data prior to loading into editor, can be either an array containing the new data, a vector containing the new column names for empty columns or a named list containing a vector for each new column.

col_edit

logical indicating whether columns can be added or removed, set to TRUE by default.

col_options

a list named with valid column names and the input to use for each column:

  • c(TRUE, FALSE): checkboxes;

  • a vector of values, e.g. c("A", "B", "C"): a dropdown menu;

  • "date" or "datetime": a date or date-time picker (the column is returned as Date or POSIXct);

  • "time": a time picker ("HH:MM" text);

  • "textarea": text over several lines;

  • "password": hidden text;

  • "url": web addresses with a button to open them;

  • "colour" (or "color"): colours shown with a swatch;

  • c(min = 0, max = 10, step = 1) (any of the three): numbers within limits;

  • "slider": a slider and bar for numbers from 0 to 100;

  • "rating": a rating from 0 to 5 stars.

Set the limits of a slider with c(type = "slider", min = 0, max = 1, step = 0.05) and the number of stars of a rating with c(type = "rating", stars = 10) (a list() works too). Values outside the limits are marked in the editor and cannot be entered. Unlike earlier versions, using col_options no longer disables adding or removing columns.

col_stretch

logical indicating whether columns should be stretched to fill the full width of the display, set to FALSE by default.

col_names

logical indicating whether column names can be edited or a vector of column names that cannot be edited, set to TRUE by default to allow editing of column names.

col_readonly

names of columns that cannot be edited. Values and names of these columns are locked in the grid.

col_hide

names of columns to hide from the editor. Hidden columns will not be visible or editable but will be retained in the data returned by the module.

col_factor

logical indicating whether character columns should be converted to factors prior to returning the edited data, set to FALSE by default.

row_bind

additional rows to add to the data prior to loading into editor, can be either an array containing the new data, a vector containing the new row names for empty rows or a named list containing a vector for each new column.

row_edit

logical indicating whether rows can be added or removed, set to TRUE by default.

row_index

retained for backwards compatibility and no longer required. Rows now carry stable identifiers, so new rows are numbered automatically.

rows

a reactive expression returning the row indices (positions in the data returned by this module) to display, or NULL to display all rows. Edits made to the displayed subset are applied directly to the full data.

columns

a reactive expression returning the names of the columns to display, or NULL to display all columns.

quiet

logical to suppress messages and notifications.

read_fun

name of the function to use to read in the data when a file is selected, set to read.csv by default.

read_args

a named list of additional arguments to pass to read_fun when reading in files.

track

can be set to TRUE to highlight cells that have been edited or added to the original data with a default blue border, or a valid CSS color (e.g. "#FF0000" or "red") to use a custom border color. Set to NULL by default to disable highlighting.

code_name

name of the data used in the code shown in the review panel, set to "data" by default. Can also be a reactive expression returning the name.

...

not in use.

Value

reactive expression containing the edited data. Pass it to dataEditCommit() to save the changes (e.g. write them to a database) and to dataEditChanges() for a summary of the changes that have not been saved yet. The reactive also carries the attribute "view", a reactive returning only the rows and columns on display.

Examples

if (interactive()) {
  library(shiny)

  ui <- fluidPage(
    dataInputUI("input-1"),
    dataOutputUI("output-1"),
    dataEditUI("edit-1")
  )

  server <- function(input, output, session) {
    data_to_edit <- dataInputServer("input-1")
    data_edit <- dataEditServer("edit-1",
      data = data_to_edit
    )
    dataOutputServer("output-1",
      data = data_edit
    )
  }

  shinyApp(ui, server)
}
